 Cameron Boozer recorded a triple-double on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, 12 assists and four three-pointers in a 124-103 win over the Trail Blazers.
 It took just five games for Boozer to record his first triple-double, and Memphis now sits at 5-0. His field goal percentage has been horrendous so far, with this being his first time shooting at least 50 percent from the floor. However, he has been excellent from the free throw line and has poured in the rebounds and assists. The shooting percentage should regulate, which will vault his fantasy value. He’s just getting started, and it won’t be long before Boozer is considered one of the premier players in fantasy basketball.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Cameron Boozer finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with 25 points (6-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers. 
 After struggling with his shot in his NBA debut on Wednesday, Boozer had a much better night against the Warriors. The rookie forward made four of his first five three-point attempts and scored 14 points in the first half. By the end of the night, Boozer had made franchise history, becoming the second-youngest Grizzly to record a double-double. Memphis ends its Week 1 with a game against the Kings on Sunday.

 Cam Boozer puts up 7 points (2-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, and 5 assists in NBA debut. 
 Do not panic about the inefficient shooting. He will not shoot 13% from the field for the rest of his career. However, we saw why many fantasy managers were very excited to have him. He got 11 rebounds and 5 assists despite the bad shooting. If he made five more of those shots, it would be an incredible stat line.

 #14 
 Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey will start Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 The Grizzlies have a new frontcourt, with Boozer, the third overall pick in last summer’s draft, and Edey, returning from a season-ending ankle injury. They’ll play prominent roles in the Grizzlies’ lineup as the franchise rebuilds after trading Jaren Jackson Jr. and Ja Morant. Jerome and Coward also offer high fantasy upside with their starting roles. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer amassed 16 points (4-of-7 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and two assists over 22 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Magic in preseason action. 
 Boozer, the third-overall pick from the 2026 NBA Draft, projects as an instantly impactful fantasy contributor in redraft leagues thanks to his unique playmaking ability and all-around skillset. The 19-year-old forward does a little bit of everything from an offensive standpoint as he’s adept at using his size to attack the basket, while also being able to knock down a handful of three-pointers. He’s a phenomenal passer and should be a factor in the rebounding department as well. Simply put, Boozer looks like the type of foundational player that Memphis should be able to rebuild around for years to come. He’s a mid-round selection with plenty of upside as a high-volume all-around contributor in redraft leagues. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer scored 11 points (5-of-9 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and two steals in 18 minutes as the Grizzlies beat the Hawks 132-123 in preseason action on Monday. 
 The Grizzlies have ostensibly turned the franchise over to Boozer, the third-overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, after moving on from both Jaren Jackson Jr. and Ja Morant in separate trades over the last few months. There are zero obstacles standing in the way of Boozer blossoming into a high-volume, all-around impact contributor for redraft leagues during his rookie campaign. There’s enough talent in his supporting cast to envision a scenario where he thrives as a playmaking facilitator that is also capable of attacking the basket with his size and strength. He certainly looked the part with Memphis rolling out nearly their full lineup with the exception of center Zach Edey in their first exhibition contest. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer totaled 19 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s summer league championship loss to the Warriors. 
 Boozer bounced back from a rough shooting performance to tie a team high in points on Sunday. He drained three triples and was solid on the boards, yet again. The No. 3 overall pick had a strong summer overall and is in line to be one of Memphis’ featured players this upcoming season. He’s got a lot of room for growth and development, but should still be a reliable contributor in fantasy leagues as a rookie.

 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer recorded 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block in Saturday’s win over the Rockets. 
 One game removed from scoring 24 points on 10-of-13 shooting, Boozer didn’t have the best day shooting the basketball against the Rockets. However, he found other ways to add value, most notably as a rebounder and facilitator. Viewed by some as a player who possesses the highest floor in this summer’s draft class, that label may be selling Boozer’s ceiling short. His ability to affect games as a scorer, rebounder and facilitator makes him one of the top fantasy rookies, and the defense should not be overlooked, either.

 Cameron Boozer amassed 24 points (10-of-13 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Thursday’s win over the Hawks. 
 Boozer and the Grizzlies needed a big win to clinch a spot in Saturday’s semifinals, and they understood the assignment from the opening tip. Memphis led 32-2 and never looked back, going on to win 96-64. Boozer made things look easy for himself against the shorthanded Hawks, scoring on all three levels and also doing some facilitating. With Memphis now in the semifinals, any thoughts about a potential shutdown for Boozer and the other summer Grizzlies who are guaranteed roles for next season can be put to rest. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer tallied 12 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Warriors. 
 Boozer didn’t have the best day shooting the basketball, but that doesn’t matter much when seven Grizzlies reach double figures in a 106-85 victory. Also, the third overall pick does not need to score to provide fantasy value, as evidenced by the rebounds, assists and steals. The Grizzlies play their fourth game in Las Vegas on Thursday, and it’s fair to wonder if Boozer will be shut down. Counting Salt Lake City, he has played a lot of basketball over the last two weeks, and there doesn’t seem to be much that the Grizzlies haven’t seen from their lottery pick. 
 Cameron Boozer 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 Cameron Boozer finished Monday’s loss to the Mavericks with 21 points (7-of-17 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers. 
 Boozer did not shoot the ball as accurately as he did in Friday’s win over the Bulls, but he had another productive day at the office. The rookie forward’s stat line was missing only a blocked shot, with a 2-of-8 effort from deep accounting for the low field-goal percentage. Boozer played well in Salt Lake City and he’s carried that over to Las Vegas. Given the amount of basketball that he’s played, the third overall pick in last month’s draft may be a prime shutdown candidate for the rest of this week.

 Portland was without Robert Williams (knee) for this game, which allowed Clingan to set a new season high for minutes. Clingan’s lack of minutes has been disappointing, but if it can continue to have between 26-30 minutes per game, he should be able to play to his fourth-round ADP, especially if he is blocking shots at this rate.

 Avdija’s production is slightly down from last season, but he continues to be the primary scoring option for Portland.  Isaiah Stewart provided a boost off the bench with 18 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one block and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Tuesday.
 Quinten Post (ankle) exited this game early, which allowed Stewart to be the primary backup center. He did most of his scoring after Post’s exit, with 15 of his 18 points coming in the second half. Stewart has been solid as a reserve for Memphis this year, though this was his season high for scoring. Unless he’s filling in for Zach Edey as a starter, Stewart shouldn’t be rostered outside of deep leagues. This level of scoring won’t come consistently.

 Fears has started all year, but with Dejounte Murray (personal) out for this game, he was able to be the primary playmaker for New Orleans, and the results were excellent. He approached triple-double territory, and the defensive stats were a huge bonus. Fears hasn’t been great this season, but he went off to help the Pelicans get their first win of the year. If Murray were to end up being traded at some point this season, Fears would likely see the usage he got in this game. That won’t lead to many performances of this level, but it should help his overall production.
